function.name: restaurant_finder
function.description: Search for restaurants based on location, cuisine type and other preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City and state, e.g. New York, NY.

cuisine.description: Type of cuisine the user is interested in, e.g. Italian, Japanese etc.

preferences.description: Extra features in the restaurant. default is ['Delivery'].

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find restaurants. We have a function to search for restaurants. The user wants two queries:

1. In New York (NY) find Italian restaurants that provide vegetarian options. So location: "New York, NY", cuisine: "Italian", preferences: "Vegetarian".

2. In Los Angeles (LA) find Japanese sushi restaurants that provide delivery service. So location: "Los Angeles, CA", cuisine: "Japanese", preferences: "Delivery".

We need to call the function twice. The function signature: restaurant_finder takes an object with location, cuisine, preferences optional. preferences can be "Vegetarian" | "Delivery" | "Vegan" | "Takeout"[].

We need to pass preferences as array? The type says preferences?: "Vegetarian" | "Delivery" | "Vegan" | "Takeout"[], but that seems ambiguous. Probably preferences is an array of strings. We'll pass array.

So first call: {location: "New York, NY", cuisine: "Italian", preferences: ["Vegetarian"]}

Second call: {location: "Los Angeles, CA", cuisine: "Japanese", preferences: ["Delivery"]}

We need to call the function twice. We'll do two calls.
